reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset and Brown note the cherubim Moses made were never condemned, since the ban targets images made for worship, not image-making itself.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells presses that a command banning any likeness of heavenly beings cannot be squared with God's own order to craft golden cherubim for the mercy seat.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible.

sides.snippet: \"You shall not make for yourselves an idol, nor any image of anything that is in the heavens above
sides.verseText: \"You shall not make for yourselves an idol, nor any image of anything that is in the heavens above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:

sides.snippet: You shall make two cherubim of hammered gold. You shall make them at the two ends of the mercy seat.
sides.verseText: You shall make two cherubim of hammered gold. You shall make them at the two ends of the mercy seat.
